pr_title: Move benchmark security to its own universe + Set default benchmark to SPY
pr_body:
#### Description
- Added new `BenchmarkUniverse` to handle the benchmark security and subscription separately from the algorithm ones
- Updated both data feeds to handle the `CollectionChanged` event for this universe
- Added a new `CustomUniverseWithBenchmarkRegressionAlgorithm`
- Updated regression stats for a couple of algorithms using `SetBenchmark`
- Set default benchmark to SPY and updated all regression statistics

#### Related Issue
Closes #2381
Closes #2260 
Closes #2299 
Closes #2153 

#### Motivation and Context
Due to the current implementation of `SetBenchmark` allowing reuse of the uninitialized benchmark security, many algorithms were behaving incorrectly (incorrect leverage used and/or no data streamed).

#### Requires Documentation Change
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
New regression algorithm + existing algorithms with the additional `SetBenchmark` call.

#### Types of changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Non-functional change (xml comments/documentation/etc)

#### Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** [document](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.
- [x] My branch follows the naming convention `bug-<issue#>-<description` or `feature-<issue#>-<description>`
pr_comments: Closing for now while we work on the [Data Feed Architecture Streamling Project](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/projects/5). This change highlighted some deficiencies in the architecture -- we'll come back to this following architecture improvements.

issue_context.title: SetBenchmark called in BasicTemplateFrameworkAlgorithm changes number of trades
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
We expect a `SetBenchmark` call in any algorithm to have no effect on the number of trades placed.

#### Actual Behavior
`SetBenchmark` changes the number of trades placed by `BasicTemplateFrameworkAlgorithm`.

#### Potential Solution
The benchmark security (which has `Leverage=1`) is being used for trades instead of the security selected by the universe selection model.

#### Reproducing the Problem
Add the following line anywhere in the `Initialize` method of  `BasicTemplateFrameworkAlgorithm`:
```
    SetBenchmark("SPY");
```
Run the algorithm: it will place **19** trades instead of **3**.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

This wasn't initially how I saw this. I was originally thinking `GetSecurity` would *always* return a non-null security, creating if necessary. Setting it up like this does absolutely work but also provides an opportunity for a discontinuity between `GetSecurity` and `CreateSecurity` -- for example, `GetSecurity` could feasibly return a different security than the one that was created using `CreateSecurity` -- I'll ping you in slack to hash this one out -- I'm think it'll be good as is but want to cover our bases.

I did it this way to ensure the existing behavior in `UniverseSelection.ApplyUniverseSelection` is unchanged, just by moving the `TryGetValue` call into `Universe.GetSecurity` -- at least for this PR didn't want to change too much :)

Check this guy https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Engine/AlgorithmManager.cs#L811

You raised an interesting point though: since these contracts expire, not sure if they can even be used as benchmarks.
